title: Housing and Division in Cities
text:
Urban housing markets reveal inequality with unusual clarity. In many cities, residents on low incomes are pushed into peripheral neighbourhoods where transport is poor and public services are thin. Such spatial segregation is rarely accidental, since zoning rules and land prices often reinforce the divisions that already exist. Over time, these patterns harden into separate worlds that seldom meet.

Planners who wish to address this problem face a dilemma. Building affordable homes near city centres can provoke resistance from existing residents, who fear declining property values or changes to local character. Yet leaving the poorest districts isolated may entrench disadvantage across generations. Many analysts therefore argue that integration should be pursued gradually, through mixed developments rather than large segregated estates.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what tends to reinforce spatial segregation?
According to paragraph two, what do existing residents fear when affordable homes are built nearby?
options: Declining property values or changes to local character

questions.text: What can be inferred about the segregation described in the passage?
options: It is mainly the result of personal choice
It is a natural and unavoidable feature of cities
It results from social and regulatory forces rather than chance

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about the approach that many analysts favour?
options: Isolating the poorest districts to protect them
Introducing change gradually through mixed developments
Ending all new construction in cities
Removing residents from city centres immediately

vocabulary.definition: the separation of groups within a society or area
located on the outer edge of an area, away from the centre
opposition to a plan, change or idea
to establish something so firmly that it is hard to change

paragraph_translations: Os mercados imobiliários urbanos revelam a desigualdade com uma clareza incomum. Em muitas cidades, moradores de baixa renda são empurrados para bairros periféricos, onde o transporte é precário e os serviços públicos são escassos. Essa segregação espacial raramente é acidental, já que as regras de zoneamento e os preços da terra costumam reforçar as divisões que já existem. Com o tempo, esses padrões se endurecem em mundos separados que raramente se encontram.

Planejadores que desejam enfrentar esse problema encaram um dilema. Construir moradias acessíveis perto dos centros urbanos pode provocar resistência dos moradores atuais, que temem a queda dos valores dos imóveis ou mudanças no caráter local. No entanto, deixar os bairros mais pobres isolados pode consolidar a desvantagem por gerações. Muitos analistas, portanto, defendem que a integração seja buscada gradualmente, por meio de empreendimentos mistos em vez de grandes conjuntos segregados.
